review: The hymn is a life-consecration: 1:1–2 is Gal 2:20 (הֶחָי … בִּי הַמָּשִׁיחַ) with 1 Cor 6:19–20, 1:3 Phil 3:8 (כִּי הַכֹּל חֵסְרוֹן), 2:3–4 Phil 3:8,14, 3:2 1 Pet 2:24, and 4:3–4 Matt 11:28 with Prov 11:30.

1:1 לְךָ נַפְשִׁי — the Arabic نَفْسِي لَكَ وَقَفْت is 'my soul I devoted to You'; the Hebrew states the dedication as a verbless possession ('my soul is Yours') rather than using the modern נֶדֶר word, since the stanza's force is ownership and the next line grounds it in the cross.

1:3 מָאַסְתִּי כֹל — the Arabic نَبَذْتُ مَا عَدَاكَ is 'I cast away all that is not You'; the Hebrew keeps the strong מָאַס (Ps 118:22, אֶבֶן מָאֲסוּ) with כֹּל rather than a comparative, so the renunciation is total and not partial.

2:2 לִרְצוֹנוֹ אֶשְׁאָפָה — the Arabic أَرُومُ رِضَاه is 'I aim at His pleasure'; שָׁאַף is the biblical verb for panting after something (Ps 42:2, כְּאַיָּל תַּעֲרֹג … תִּשְׁתּוֹמֵם), and the cohortative keeps the resolve of the Arabic imperfect.

3:1 מַר־מָוֶת — the Arabic ذَاقَ الْمُرَّ الْمُذِيب is 'tasted the dissolving bitter thing'; the Hebrew compresses it into the construct מַר־מָוֶת because the stanza is four lines of eight to ten syllables, and מַר is the biblical word for the bitter cup (1 Sam 15:32, מַר־הַמָּוֶת).
